fields.title: Typed flags and kill-switch control plane
fields.description:
Delivery epic: downstream Batter applications stop hand-rolling feature flags from environment variables and declare typed flags and kill switches once, in code.

Canonical plan: `.agent/plans/flags-control-plane.md` (Critical profile, proposed 2026-11-04, repository baseline fb83054). It is a gitignored file in the checkout of the design session's machine; the child beads carry their own task text, and §4 (design) lives only in that file. Status: proposed; ADR-016 acceptance by the owner (T-01) is the first gate.

## 1. Outcome

Downstream Batter applications stop hand-rolling feature flags from environment variables.
They declare every flag and kill switch once, in code, as typed handles in one catalog, and
evaluate them only through those handles. Work evaluates through one view per HTTP request, job
invocation or periodic run; the application may pin a decision into its own domain row and
replay it on retry (R-09); kill switches gate route groups, job types and periodic components
with library-owned responses. Two sources feed that one evaluation model:

1. Declared mode (Phase 1; no new infrastructure): values resolved once at startup from the
   application's existing `SettingsSource`, with strict literals, closed-state absence,
   process-kind ownership, retired names and development-only restrictions enforced by the
   library, and value-free diagnostics. A value changes by changing its setting and restarting.
2. Control-plane mode (Phases 2-3; owner-selected scope): an audited PostgreSQL control plane
   whose versioned snapshot a registered Batter component loads and refreshes, so flags and
   switches change without a redeploy; a last-good file for restarts during an outage; a fleet
   view from per-process heartbeats; a small operator CLI with compare-and-set writes; and, in
   Phase 3, push wake-ups, per-subject rollouts and control-plane invariant checks.

Completion signals:

- `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes on Rust 1.98.1 with all new packages, features, examples and
  inventories, and the outcome is recorded in the owning bead.
- The `rollout` facade example demonstrates declared mode, a gated route group, a per-request
  view, a pinned job decision and (with `DATABASE_URL`) the control plane; its DB-free tests run
  in the ordinary matrix.
- The single-facade consumer prints each new marker exactly once against PostgreSQL 18: Phase 1
  (declared catalog resolved, pinned decision stored in row, gated job type deferred) and Phase 2
  (loaded before readiness, held entry kept last good, pinned decision executed, kill switch
  overrode a pin, heartbeat recorded build and version).
- Every ignored PostgreSQL 18 suite the tasks add passes on an explicit `--ignored` run whose
  command and result are recorded on the owning bead; the new `native-runflag-postgres` hosted
  job has a recorded run URL.
- Fresh-agent evaluations 1 and 2 (T-22, T-24) ran against their frozen oracles, with scored
  decisions and logs archived under `docs/evidence/`. An evaluation the owner defers is closed as
  deferred with that decision quoted on the epic, stays labelled proposed and unexecuted, and
  does not count as met.
- ADR-016, the ADR-010 assessment sections, status rows, experimental labels and
  `docs/references.md` entries exist and agree with the shipped API.

## 2. Scope

In scope: everything in §4 (Design) and the tasks in §5, in three phases plus close-out.

Non-goals (recorded so they are not rebuilt by accident):

- Statsig, OpenFeature or any vendor/remote source behind the handles: no public provider trait,
  source adapter or vendor mapping, and no watch-list row (owner decision). runflag-core's
  disclosed `low_level` publication path (§4.1) accepts validated candidates from any caller; it
  is a weaker escape hatch, not a provider interface, and adding a trait or adapter would reopen
  ADR-014's rejection of a generic provider interface
  (`docs/adr/014-reuse-after-two-consumers.md:54-57`).
- Experiment analysis, exposure-based statistics, dashboards, approval workflows, RBAC.
- A second settings system: settings (URLs, secrets, timeouts, pool sizes, `JOBS_*`) stay in
  `batter::settings`; nothing is added to that module (`crates/batter-core/src/settings.rs:3-6`).
- Native Runledger edits (claim-time gating) while `batter-05ci` owns the worker files.
- Executing deployments, drains or stop-writer windows; Batter declares and verifies, it does
  not orchestrate infrastructure.
- Windows; non-Unix fallbacks (ADR-007).
- Committing, pushing or publishing; those need a separate owner instruction.

Constraints: Rust 1.98.1 and `rust-version = "1.98.1"` everywhere; PostgreSQL 18 minimum for
Batter integrations (`docs/integrations.md:12-13`); zero boolean parameters on public APIs
(`clippy.toml:3`, `Cargo.toml:32`); every `.rs` file the plan adds or edits stays ≤ 800 lines
(`.jig/file-budget.toml:3-8,57`); generic scenario names; every new public API passes the
ADR-010 five-question review (`docs/adr/010-agent-only-consumption.md:52-75`); every claim is
tested or labelled unverified; every public hard cut ships `Breaking:` + `Migration:` + shim
decision checked against the public-API diff method; external semantics recorded in
`docs/references.md`.


## Shared rules for every task (plan §5)

Shared rules for every task: claim the task's bead (filed by T-01) before starting; work on a
branch (never on `master` directly); every new public item has rustdoc, an example and its ADR-010
assessment entry; every claim is tested or labelled unverified; test code that reads the process environment
(child-root markers, test database URLs) lives under `tests/` or in a file that only a
`#[cfg(test)]` module declaration loads, never in an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod` block of a
production file, so T-03's scan does not count it (T-06, T-12, T-14, T-15); every new or changed
`.rs` file
stays ≤ 800 lines (`.jig/file-budget.toml`); no boolean parameters; generic scenario names; record
the verification outcome as a bead comment; a task that changes code, a manifest or a script runs
`bash scripts/verify.sh` once on Rust 1.98.1 after its focused checks pass and before its bead
closes (AGENTS.md "Done Means", §6); committing, pushing and publishing still need an
explicit owner request. Parallel lanes add to shared documents (`CHANGELOG.md`,
`docs/guarantees.md`, `docs/status.md`, `docs/adr/010-agent-only-consumption.md`) only under a
task-named entry or subsection and resolve conflicts on rebase.

Hot spots (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, every member's dependency and feature tables,
`crates/batter/Cargo.toml`, `crates/batter/src/lib.rs`, `scripts/check_facade_features.py`,
`scripts/test_matrix.py`, `scripts/test_parallel_process.py`, `scripts/verify.sh`,
`scripts/test_verify.py`, `scripts/ci_plan.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
`crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs`, AGENTS.md counts) are edited only by T-02, T-03,
T-11, T-17 and T-25. T-02 declares every dependency and feature later tasks use, so any other lane
leaves `Cargo.lock` unchanged (every `--locked` command fails otherwise) and hands a missing edge to
the next owner. No hot-spot case references an item a later task introduces. The task that changes
a count updates every sentence stating it. Other tasks touch their own package and documentation.

## Critical path, owner gates and parallel lanes (plan §5)

Critical path: T-01 → T-02 → T-04 → T-05 → T-12 → T-13 → T-14 → T-15 → T-17 → T-20 → T-21 →
T-25; T-05 → T-06 → {T-08, T-09, T-10} → T-14 is equally long.

Owner gates on that path: ADR-016 acceptance, answers 5 and 9, T-01's dated crates.io check and the
merge of the concurrent TLS work (before T-02); answers 1, 2 and 7 (before T-12 writes its
migration); a push authorization for the hosted `native-runflag-postgres` run (T-17); answer 4
(T-20 runs or closes as excluded).

Parallel lanes: T-03, T-07 and T-18 start right after T-02; T-12 and T-13 run beside T-06..T-11
once T-05 is done; T-08, T-09 and T-10 run together after T-06; T-16 runs beside T-14 and T-15
after T-13; after T-17, T-19 and T-20 run together and T-21 follows T-20; T-22 (after T-11), T-23
and T-24 run beside Phase 3. Forward migrations after T-12 come only from T-13, T-20 and T-21,
which are serialized, so no two tasks claim the same `schema_revision`.

## Owner questions (safe defaults shown; answers recorded on the epic by T-01)

1. Environment scoping of flags. Default: unscoped flags, one schema per environment;
   `environment` stays a heartbeat label. Needed before T-12 writes its migration.
2. Ledger placement. Default: default schema, `flag_` prefix, shared ledger with
   `set_ignore_missing(true)` and vendoring consts. Needed before T-12 writes its migration.
3. `HttpFailure::Disabled` as a permanent hard cut. Default: accept, no shim. Needed before T-07
   merges.
4. Per-subject rollouts in this epic despite 0/3 consumer evidence. Default: include as T-20.
5. Family and binary name `runflag`. Default: as written, provided T-01's dated crates.io check
   finds `runflag`, `runflag-core`, `runflag-postgres`, `runflag-cli` and `batter-flags` available.
   Needed before T-02.
6. Toggle spelling. Default: `ToggleLiterals` chosen per catalog, `TrueFalse` recommended for
   migrated catalogs.
7. Native store dependency. Default: sqlx only, with a native `CommitOutcomeUnknown` type (no
   `batter-sqlx` dependency in the native family). Needed before T-12 writes its migration.
8. Publishing `runflag-cli`. Default: `publish = false` until the release-train record.
9. An in-repo-authored native family (`runflag/`) instead of `crates/` leaves. Default: native family,
   including the 0.1.0 version line and per-package MIT license copies for runflag-core,
   runflag-postgres and runflag-cli, recorded in ADR-016 and an ADR-006 amendment. Needed before
   T-02.
10. ADR-014's reopening condition (one consumer now composes through the lifecycle layer).
    Default: note in ADR-016, propose a separate re-survey bead.
11. Development-only (`only_in`) flags are declared-only and never writable through the control
    plane. Default: yes.
12. Phase order. Default: survey-evidenced items (invariants R-05, revision R-10, job gate R-19,
    pins R-09) in Phase 1 before the owner-selected control plane and per-subject rollouts; R-08 is
    deferred to its follow-up bead, as are bounded integers (rest of R-03) and R-15 (§3.1, §5).


## Follow-ups

The plan's follow-up beads are linked discovered-from this epic. They are evidenced or blocked work outside this epic's completion.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Every completion signal in plan §1 (listed in this description) is recorded on this epic with its evidence by T-25; the owner's §8.2 answers are quoted on this epic.
fields.design:
Architecture at a glance (plan §4; the full design, alternatives and evidence are in the plan file).

Packages:
- `runflag/runflag-core` (native, 0.1.0, MIT): catalog grammar, `ReleaseFlag<T>` (mandatory expiry), `ModeFlag<T>`, `KillSwitch` (`SafeState`, `StaleRule`), handles, digests and manifest, validated `Snapshot`, `SnapshotView`, `Decision`/`Reason`/`Source`, evaluation that reads no clock, exposure and load events, the `Pinned<T>` envelope and `PinnedResolution`, a disclosed `low_level` publication path. No tokio, sqlx or axum in its normal closure.
- `runflag/runflag-postgres` (native, 0.1.0, MIT): schema and forward-only migrations, audited compare-and-set writes with exhaustive outcomes, history, archive/restore, catalog publication, presence heartbeats, prune and the fleet query.
- `runflag/runflag-cli` (native binary `runflag`, `publish = false`): operator commands with compare-and-set writes and a JSON scripting contract.
- `crates/batter-flags` (adapter): declared mode (`declared::resolve` → `Resolved` → `Flags`), `control_plane::register_in` (feature `postgres`), loader, last-good file, readiness condition `flags.snapshot`, HTTP gate builders and `AdmittedFlags` (`axum`), job handler wrappers and `JobFlags` (`runledger`), periodic gate, `TestFlags`, `low_level::capture_now`.
- `crates/batter-axum`: flags-agnostic route-group gate seam (`GroupGate`, `Gated`, `GateView`) and `HttpFailure::Disabled` (503, code `disabled`), a permanent public hard cut.
- `crates/batter-core`: additive experimental `periodic::register_wakeable_in` (Phase 3).
- Facade features `flags`, `flags-postgres`, `flags-axum`, `flags-runledger`; namespaces `batter::flags::{native, postgres, control_plane, http, jobs, periodic, low_level, test}`.

Dependency direction: no runflag package depends on any `batter-*`, `runledger-*` or `runlimit-*` package; only batter-flags has normal edges into runflag; batter-core, batter-axum and batter-runledger never depend on runflag or batter-flags; batter-flags never depends on the facade.
